newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: British-owned shop chain attacked in Lithuania.
newsitem.headline: British-owned shop chain attacked in Lithuania.

text.p: A British-owned chain of shops was hit by bomb blasts in three Lithuanian cities in what was believed to be a revenge attack for refusal to pay protection money, the interior ministry said on Tuesday.

Noone was hurt in the attacks on three Vision Express opticians shops, which took place almost simultaneously around one o'clock in the morning (2200 GMT) on Sunday in the capital Vilnius, the second city Kaunas and the northern town of Panevezhys.
The attacks are part of a wave of organised crime, which has soared in Lithuania and the other two Baltic states of Latvia and Estonia since they quit the former Soviet Union in 1991.
"The preliminary findings are that 'security' was proposed to these shops and they refused," an interior ministry spokesman told Reuters.
The shops suffered varying damage, with the outlet in Panevezhys hit worst as its doors and windows were blown out.

He said that at the scene of the blast in Kaunas a grenade ring was found. One man was arrested in Vilnius, who was believed to be a resident of Panevezhys. The town is seen as a hotbed of organised crime where gang shoot-outs are quite common.
